decision.evidence: Accepted original-Alpha F3 and terminal-optimality repair after current proof review. F3 now states only existence/uniqueness actually supplied; direct strict quadratic expansion certifies any terminal tuple. Independent old rows force the next direction after deleting a negative multiplier to be nonzero; strict descent prevents face-minimum recurrence, and positive steps bound episodes by 2^m and iterations by (n+2)2^m. Same defect as refuter85:4, preserving its existing identity and history.
decision.same_defect_evidence: This stabilized carrier records the very same original Alpha proof/citation amendment already resolving refuter:85:4; the archived report, current proof and existing closed defect row identify the same locus and correction.

decision.evidence: F3 inflated the existence lemma to universal KKT sufficiency. Corrected the fact to actual existence/uniqueness and proved terminal global optimality directly by stationarity/complementarity and strict quadratic expansion. Also made explicit why deleting a negative-multiplier row gives a nonzero next direction, using uniqueness of independent-row multiplier representations. Strict descent, blocker independence, no face-minimum recurrence, at most 2^m episodes and n-r+2 iteration bound are valid under the stated positive-step hypothesis.

target.evidence: [F3] attributes the claim that “any feasible KKT tuple is a global certificate” to lem-sqp-convex-quadratic-subproblem-has-unique-kkt-certificate. That lemma’s Statement asserts existence of multipliers at its unique minimizer and says “This KKT tuple certifies the global minimizer”; it does not state sufficiency for every feasible KKT tuple. Step 4.1 uses the stronger universal claim for the algorithm’s terminal tuple.
